question: Do the 2016 and 2017 signed-message bodies become prime-length GP-rune streams when F is omitted?
source: Supplied numerical discussion, attachment 4d80ab80-eab0-4f0d-b595-68e0167eb871; source SHA-256 e7f90ade745e6367b90a8bffe83e68f92f7ec316f60ad7be409ec9f876deed3b
corpus: The preserved 2016 extracted signed message and 2017 signed message in the later-message manifest; count only bodies before PGP SIGNATURE armor.
transliteration: ASCII letter runs, uppercase, V mapped to U, shortest unique encoding under stored GP aliases, as declared in scripts/later_message_sums.py.
control: Apply the same one-symbol omission to each of the 29 GP rune indices and list every symbol whose removal leaves prime lengths in both messages. This is a conditional count over a fixed alphabet, not a p-value.
exclusions: Alternate transliterations, sentence splitting, GP sums, other source messages, author intent or an LP2 decryption.
